messages:
jess (sales): Customer (large telco) asks about air-gapped POC feasibility. Main asks: installer packaging, delta upgrades offline, license binding to HW ID, and an outline of pricing for 4-week eval + conversion discounts. Any quick red flags?

harry (solutions): We can create a single signed bundle and then produce signed delta artifacts for subsequent patches. Deltas are smaller but require exact base bundle-id.

lia (eng): Preflight check mandatory. We need kernel, glibc, nvidia driver version, container runtime, and available RAM/disk. If drivers mismatch we can use a compat container but lose performance.

frank (security): Offline license: signed token with hwid or hostname allowed. Installer verifies signature using our public key. We recommend customers use an HSM for key storage; we provide PKCS#11 compatibility. Also need completed security questionnaire before delivery.

amy (cs): Pricing: POC flat fee (example $25k for 4 wks inc 4 support hours), per-node reserved pricing if they commit. Setup/transfer assistance is extra. If they convert within 60 days we credit POC fee.

jess (sales): Who owns upgrade push? We can't initiate outbound updates into their network right?

lia (eng): Correct — we supply signed artifacts only. If they want us to perform updates we offer a managed-update option where they either open a temporary egress or we run an update via their bastion.

harry (solutions): Action items: sample preflight script + bundle template (lia), sample signed token & activation flow (frank), draft POC quote (amy). Aim EOD Tue.

deploy-bot: Ticket TG-3344 created: "airgapped poc packaging + license" assigned lia/harry/amy due 2026-04-15.

jess (sales): I'll send customer an inventory template and export-control checklist. Thanks!"
